title: Multiple Representations of Relationships

authority.learning_target: Students will connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
authority.intro: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
authority.review: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.
authority.mastery: Solve inequalities, represent solution sets graphically, and interpret solutions in context.

math_note_ideas: Equivalent representations preserve the same input-output pairs even when they look different.
Use two checkpoints to test equivalence: a shared ordered pair and a shared rate/pattern.
Scale changes appearance, not the underlying relationship.
figure_representation_ideas: coordinate graph paired with a small value table
context graph with labeled axes and meaningful units

title: Inputs, Outputs, and Functions

authority.learning_target: Students will interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
authority.intro: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
authority.review: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.
authority.mastery: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions correctly using substitution and order of operations.

math_note_ideas: A function assigns exactly one output to each input.
Input/output is a relationship role, not automatically x/y until defined.
Function rules can be evaluated forward and reasoned backward when output is known.

title: Function Families

authority.learning_target: Students will recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
authority.intro: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
authority.review: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.
authority.mastery: Accurately perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals while interpreting results in mathematical and contextual situations.

math_note_ideas: Linear: constant first difference; quadratic: constant second difference; exponential: constant multiplicative ratio.
Absolute-value graphs have a vertex and two linear arms; shape alone should be checked against equation/table structure.
Family classification should use at least two forms of evidence when ambiguity is possible.
figure_representation_ideas: compare parabola and exponential growth on same window

title: Expressions and Structure

authority.learning_target: Students will interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
authority.intro: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
authority.review: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.
authority.mastery: Analyze and rewrite algebraic expressions using properties of operations and algebraic structure.

math_note_ideas: Equivalent expressions have the same value for every allowed input.
Structure means seeing grouped quantities, factors, sums, and repeated pieces before calculating.
The distributive property connects area/rectangle models to symbolic expansion.

title: Equations as Models

authority.learning_target: Students will write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
authority.intro: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
authority.review: Represent linear relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and contextual descriptions.
authority.mastery: Solve one-variable equations and interpret solutions within mathematical and contextual situations.

math_note_ideas: An equation states that two expressions represent the same quantity.
Modeling requires defining the variable and interpreting the solution, not only solving.
Operations used to solve should preserve equality.
figure_representation_ideas: bar model for start fee + repeated rate = total

title: Rate of Change and Slope

authority.learning_target: Students will interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
authority.intro: Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
authority.review: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
authority.mastery: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.

math_note_ideas: Slope is change in output divided by change in input.
Slope units come from vertical units per horizontal units.
Any two points on a straight line give the same slope.
figure_representation_ideas: two lines with different positive/negative/zero slopes

title: Graphing Linear Functions

authority.learning_target: Students will graph linear functions and interpret key features.
authority.intro: Graph linear functions and interpret key features.
authority.review: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
authority.mastery: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.

math_note_ideas: In y=mx+b, m controls rate/direction and b locates the y-intercept.
A graph is a set of ordered-pair solutions, not a picture disconnected from the equation.
figure_representation_ideas: line with slope triangle and intercept label

title: Writing Linear Equations

authority.learning_target: Students will write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
authority.intro: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
authority.review: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
authority.mastery: Represent linear relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and contextual descriptions.

math_note_ideas: Choose a form that matches the information you are given.
Two points determine the slope of a nonvertical line; one point plus slope determines the line.
figure_representation_ideas: context graph with initial value visible

title: Comparing Linear Representations

authority.learning_target: Students will analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.
authority.intro: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.
authority.review: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
authority.mastery: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.

math_note_ideas: Compare linear relationships by invariant features such as rate and starting value, not appearance alone.
Different representations can be translated to common features for comparison.
figure_representation_ideas: two linear graphs with intentionally different scales

title: Linear Modeling with Data

authority.learning_target: Students will use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
authority.intro: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
authority.review: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
authority.mastery: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.

math_note_ideas: A linear model summarizes a trend; data points do not need to lie exactly on the line.
Interpolation stays inside the observed x-range; extrapolation extends beyond it and is less certain.
figure_representation_ideas: scatter plot with line of fit
two candidate trend lines on same scatter plot

title: Graphing and Elimination

authority.learning_target: Students will solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
authority.intro: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
authority.review: Graph linear functions and interpret key features.
authority.mastery: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.

math_note_ideas: A system solution satisfies both equations simultaneously.
Parallel distinct lines give no solution; same line gives infinitely many solutions.
Elimination preserves the solution set when equations are combined correctly.

title: Solving Systems by Substitution

authority.learning_target: Students will solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
authority.intro: Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
authority.review: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
authority.mastery: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.

math_note_ideas: Substitution replaces a quantity with an equal expression.
Efficient substitution uses a form already solved for a variable or easy to isolate.
figure_representation_ideas: system equations with one equation highlighted as substitution-ready

title: Writing and Solving Systems from Situations

authority.learning_target: Students will create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
authority.intro: Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
authority.review: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
authority.mastery: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.

math_note_ideas: Each equation should encode one independent condition.
Solutions must satisfy the algebra and the real-world constraints.
figure_representation_ideas: table showing two quantities and shared total constraints

title: Graphing Linear Inequalities

authority.learning_target: Students will graph and interpret linear inequalities.
authority.intro: Graph and interpret linear inequalities.
authority.review: Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
authority.mastery: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.

math_note_ideas: The boundary line separates points that satisfy from points that do not.
Use a solid boundary for <= or >= and dashed for < or >.
A test point determines which half-plane is included when not obvious.
figure_representation_ideas: four inequality graphs with varied boundary/shading

title: Linear Systems of Inequalities

authority.learning_target: Students will analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
authority.intro: Analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
authority.review: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.
authority.mastery: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.

math_note_ideas: A system of inequalities is satisfied where all individual solution regions overlap.
Feasible points must satisfy every constraint.

title: Recognizing Function Families

authority.learning_target: Students will identify common function families from graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
authority.intro: Identify common function families from graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
authority.review: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
authority.mastery: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.

math_note_ideas: Function-family evidence can come from rate patterns, equation structure, or graph features.
Do not classify from shape alone when window/scale can mislead.

title: Translations

authority.learning_target: Students will graph and write translated functions using key points and key features.
authority.intro: Graph and write translated functions using key points and key features.
authority.review: Graph and interpret linear inequalities.
authority.mastery: Graph linear functions and interpret key features.

math_note_ideas: Outside addition changes outputs vertically; inside changes inputs horizontally with opposite sign behavior.
Track key points to understand translations rather than memorizing pictures.

title: Transformations

authority.learning_target: Students will analyze and graph transformations involving stretches, compressions, and reflections.
authority.intro: Analyze and graph transformations involving stretches, compressions, and reflections.
authority.review: Analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.
authority.mastery: Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.

math_note_ideas: Multiplying outputs changes vertical scale; changing the input changes horizontal scale inversely.
Negative factors can reflect a graph.

title: Polynomial Operations

authority.learning_target: Students will add, subtract, and multiply polynomial expressions.
authority.intro: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomial expressions.
authority.review: Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
authority.mastery: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.

math_note_ideas: Like terms have identical variable parts.
Polynomial multiplication is repeated distribution; area models make every product visible.

title: Polynomial Structure and Quadratic Graphs

authority.learning_target: Students will connect polynomial expressions to quadratic graphs and key features.
authority.intro: Connect polynomial expressions to quadratic graphs and key features.
authority.review: Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
authority.mastery: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.

math_note_ideas: Quadratic structure can be read symbolically and graphically; coefficients affect shape and position.
Graph features should be justified from form, not guessed from appearance.

title: GCF and Structure

authority.learning_target: Students will identify common factors and use structure to rewrite polynomial expressions.
authority.intro: Identify common factors and use structure to rewrite polynomial expressions.
authority.review: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomial expressions.
authority.mastery: Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.

math_note_ideas: Factoring reverses distribution.
The GCF should divide every term and leave an expression with no remaining common factor.

title: Factoring Trinomials

authority.learning_target: Students will factor quadratic trinomials using patterns, products, sums, and structure.
authority.intro: Factor quadratic trinomials using patterns, products, sums, and structure.
authority.review: Connect polynomial expressions to quadratic graphs and key features.
authority.mastery: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.

math_note_ideas: Factoring seeks expressions whose product recreates every term.
Product sign and sum sign constrain factor signs.

title: Special Factoring Patterns

authority.learning_target: Students will recognize and factor special polynomial patterns.
authority.intro: Recognize and factor special polynomial patterns.
authority.review: Identify common function families from graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
authority.mastery: Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.

math_note_ideas: Special patterns are consequences of polynomial multiplication, not isolated tricks.
Check both the first/last terms and the middle-term condition.
figure_representation_ideas: side-by-side area models for special products

title: Factored Form and Zeros

authority.learning_target: Students will connect factors, zeros, intercepts, and graphs of quadratic functions.
authority.intro: Connect factors, zeros, intercepts, and graphs of quadratic functions.
authority.review: Graph and write translated functions using key points and key features.
authority.mastery: Graph and interpret linear inequalities.

math_note_ideas: A zero of a function is an input that makes the output zero; on the graph it is an x-intercept.
Factored form makes zeros visible.

title: Comparing Quadratic Forms

authority.learning_target: Students will compare standard, vertex, and factored forms of quadratic functions and determine which form best reveals key features.
authority.intro: Compare standard, vertex, and factored forms of quadratic functions and determine which form best reveals key features.
authority.review: Analyze and graph transformations involving stretches, compressions, and reflections.
authority.mastery: Analyze and interpret systems of linear inequalities.

math_note_ideas: Equivalent quadratic forms reveal different features efficiently.
Choose form based on the question being asked.
figure_representation_ideas: same parabola annotated with features linked to forms

title: Solving Quadratics by Factoring

authority.learning_target: Students will solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.
authority.intro: Solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.
authority.review: Connect factors, zeros, intercepts, and graphs of quadratic functions.
authority.mastery: Connect polynomial expressions to quadratic graphs and key features.

math_note_ideas: The zero-product property applies only when a product equals zero.
Set the equation to zero before factoring when necessary.
figure_representation_ideas: parabola crossing x-axis at factored roots

title: Completing the Square

authority.learning_target: Students will solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.
authority.intro: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.
authority.review: Compare standard, vertex, and factored forms of quadratic functions and determine which form best reveals key features.
authority.mastery: Graph and write translated functions using key points and key features.

math_note_ideas: To complete x^2+bx, add (b/2)^2.
Completing the square preserves equality when the same amount is added to both sides.
The process creates vertex form structure.

title: Quadratic Formula

authority.learning_target: Students will solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.
authority.intro: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.
authority.review: Identify common factors and use structure to rewrite polynomial expressions.
authority.mastery: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomial expressions.

math_note_ideas: The quadratic formula solves ax^2+bx+c=0 for a≠0.
The discriminant b^2-4ac predicts the number of real solutions.

title: Choosing and Defending Solution Methods

authority.learning_target: Students will compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.
authority.intro: Compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.
authority.review: Recognize and factor special polynomial patterns.
authority.mastery: Identify common function families from graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.

math_note_ideas: Method choice depends on structure: factorability, square form, coefficients, and desired exactness.
Different correct methods should agree on the same solutions.

title: Quadratic Modeling and Optimization

authority.learning_target: Students will use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.
authority.intro: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.
authority.review: Factor quadratic trinomials using patterns, products, sums, and structure.
authority.mastery: Analyze and graph transformations involving stretches, compressions, and reflections.

math_note_ideas: The vertex represents a maximum or minimum when the model is quadratic.
Context determines which part of the parabola and which roots are meaningful.
figure_representation_ideas: projectile or area parabola with context axes

title: Recognizing Growth and Decay

authority.learning_target: Students will identify exponential relationships from patterns, tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.intro: Identify exponential relationships from patterns, tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.review: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.
authority.mastery: Recognize and factor special polynomial patterns.

math_note_ideas: Exponential relationships multiply by a constant factor over equal input intervals.
Growth factor >1; decay factor between 0 and 1.

title: Writing Exponential Equations

authority.learning_target: Students will write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.intro: Write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.review: Solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.
authority.mastery: Identify common factors and use structure to rewrite polynomial expressions.

math_note_ideas: a is the value at x=0 in the basic model; b is the multiplier per one input unit.
Percent change and growth factor are related but not the same number.
figure_representation_ideas: exponential graph with initial value highlighted

title: Graphing and Analyzing Exponential Functions

authority.learning_target: Students will graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
authority.intro: Graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
authority.review: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.
authority.mastery: Connect factors, zeros, intercepts, and graphs of quadratic functions.

math_note_ideas: Exponential graphs change multiplicatively and typically approach but do not cross the horizontal baseline in basic models.
The base controls growth/decay rate.
figure_representation_ideas: multiple exponential curves with common initial value

title: Comparing Function Families

authority.learning_target: Students will compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
authority.intro: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
authority.review: Compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.
authority.mastery: Compare standard, vertex, and factored forms of quadratic functions and determine which form best reveals key features.

math_note_ideas: Different families can look similar over a small interval; use pattern structure and multiple representations.

title: Exponential Modeling with Data

authority.learning_target: Students will create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
authority.intro: Create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
authority.review: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.
authority.mastery: Factor quadratic trinomials using patterns, products, sums, and structure.

math_note_ideas: An exponential model assumes approximately constant multiplicative change over equal intervals.
Model parameters should have contextual meaning.

title: Selecting Appropriate Models

authority.learning_target: Students will determine whether a situation is best modeled by a linear, quadratic, or exponential function.
authority.intro: Determine whether a situation is best modeled by a linear, quadratic, or exponential function.
authority.review: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
authority.mastery: Compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.

math_note_ideas: Model selection should use structure in the data, not only graph appearance.
No model is automatically correct outside the observed domain.
figure_representation_ideas: same data with three candidate model curves

title: Transformations Across Function Families

authority.learning_target: Students will analyze transformations across multiple function families.
authority.intro: Analyze transformations across multiple function families.
authority.review: Graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
authority.mastery: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.

math_note_ideas: Transformation notation should be interpreted consistently across function families while respecting each parent function.

title: Absolute Value Functions and Piecewise Thinking

authority.learning_target: Students will analyze and model situations involving absolute value functions.
authority.intro: Analyze and model situations involving absolute value functions.
authority.review: Identify exponential relationships from patterns, tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.mastery: Solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.

math_note_ideas: Absolute value represents distance from zero or from a target after a shift.
The vertex marks the minimum distance/value in basic absolute-value models.

title: Modeling Investigation

authority.learning_target: Students will create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
authority.intro: Create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
authority.review: Create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
authority.mastery: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.

math_note_ideas: A modeling cycle includes defining quantities, choosing a model, checking fit, interpreting parameters, and revising if necessary.
figure_representation_ideas: data scatter plot with candidate model

title: Function Synthesis and Capstone Analysis

authority.learning_target: Students will synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
authority.intro: Synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
authority.review: Write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.mastery: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.

math_note_ideas: Synthesis means choosing and connecting tools, not merely performing every procedure in the course.
Evidence should be communicated with equations, tables, graphs, and contextual interpretation as appropriate.
